cards.front: Which five possessive adjectives does this lesson give, with their meanings?
cards.answer: mein (my) / dein (your) / sein (his) / ihr (her/their) / unser (our)

cards.front: What are the six relationship status words given for describing family members?
items: in einer zivilen Partnerschaft (in a civil partnership)
cards.answer: verheiratet (married) / geschieden (divorced) / getrennt (separated) / ledig (single) / in einer Beziehung (in a relationship) / in einer zivilen Partnerschaft (in a civil partnership)

cards.front: Why does mein change to meinen in 'In meiner Familie gibt es meinen Vater'?
cards.answer: Es gibt always takes the accusative case, which changes mein to meinen before a masculine noun.

cards.front: How does word order change in a relative clause like 'Ich habe einen Bruder, der Tom heißt'?
cards.answer: The relative pronoun (der, die or das) must match the noun's gender, and the verb moves to the end of the clause.

cards.front: What are the six forms of sein (to be) in the preterite tense?
cards.answer: ich war / du warst / er/sie/es war / wir waren / ihr wart / sie/Sie waren

cards.front: What are the six forms of werden used to build the future tense?
cards.answer: ich werde / du wirst / er/sie/es wird / wir werden / ihr werdet / sie/Sie werden

cards.front: Why do verbs like fahren and fliegen use sein rather than haben in the perfect tense?
cards.answer: Verbs of movement, such as fahren and fliegen, form the perfect tense with sein instead of haben.

cards.front: What happens to the verb's position in a sentence after weil or obwohl?
cards.answer: After weil or obwohl, the verb moves to the end of the clause instead of staying in second position.

cards.front: What are the three adverbs for expressing how much you like an activity, from least to most?
cards.answer: gern (like doing) / lieber (prefer doing) / am liebsten (like doing most)

cards.front: What are the six regular present-tense verb endings, matched to their pronoun?
cards.answer: ich → -e / du → -st / er/sie/es → -t / wir → -en / ihr → -t / sie/Sie → -en

cards.front: How do you find the stem of a regular verb like spielen before adding an ending?
cards.answer: Remove -en from the infinitive to get the stem, such as spiel- from spielen, then add the correct ending.

cards.front: How do you say you don't like doing something, based on the word gern?
cards.answer: Add nicht before gern, as in 'Ich schwimme nicht gern' (I don't like swimming).

cards.front: Which relative pronoun matches each type of noun: masculine, feminine/plural, and neuter?
cards.answer: der (masculine) / die (feminine/plural) / das (neuter)

cards.front: What are the four frequency intensifiers given for describing personality, from always to never?
cards.answer: immer (always) / manchmal (sometimes) / oft (often) / nie (never)

cards.front: How is a relative clause punctuated and ordered, as in 'Mein Vater, der sehr geduldig ist, hilft mir'?
cards.answer: A comma comes before the relative pronoun, and the verb of the relative clause moves to the end.

cards.front: How do you form the comparative of an adjective like alt, jung or groß?
cards.answer: Add -er to the adjective and use als (than); alt, jung and groß also add an Umlaut in the comparative.

cards.front: How do you work out the gender of a German compound noun like das Einzelzimmer?
cards.answer: The last word in a German compound noun sets its gender, so Einzel + das Zimmer becomes das Einzelzimmer.

cards.front: Why is 'Ich möchte' used instead of 'Ich will' when booking a hotel room?
cards.answer: Möchte (would like) is more polite than will (want) for making a request, such as booking a room.

cards.front: What are the four reasons for doing sport given using um...zu phrases?
items: um fit zu bleiben (to stay fit)
um gesünder zu werden (to become healthier)
um Spaß zu haben (to have fun)
cards.answer: um fit zu bleiben (to stay fit) / um gesünder zu werden (to become healthier) / um sich zu entspannen (to relax) / um Spaß zu haben (to have fun)

cards.front: Which five sport verbs does this lesson give as using sein (not haben) in the perfect tense?
cards.answer: schwimmen (to swim) / laufen (to run) / Rad fahren (to cycle) / klettern (to climb) / reiten (to ride)

cards.front: Why do many sport verbs, such as schwimmen and laufen, use sein rather than haben in the perfect tense?
cards.answer: They are verbs of movement or change of state, moving from one place to another, so they take sein.

cards.front: How does the um...zu construction work in a sentence like 'Ich schwimme, um in Form zu bleiben'?
cards.answer: Um...zu means 'in order to', and the infinitive verb goes to the end of the phrase.

cards.front: What are the four common preposition-plus-article contractions given in this lesson?
cards.answer: in dem = im / an dem = am / zu dem = zum / zu der = zur

cards.front: How do the definite articles change in the dative case?
cards.answer: der/das → dem / die → der / die (plural) → den + n

cards.front: Why does 'in' take the dative in 'Ich bin in dem Hotel' but the accusative in 'Ich gehe in das Hotel'?
cards.answer: Two-way prepositions take the dative for location, where something is, and the accusative for movement towards a place.

cards.front: Why does 'der Zug' become 'dem Zug' in the phrase 'mit dem Zug'?
cards.answer: Mit always takes the dative case, which changes der to dem for masculine and neuter nouns.

cards.front: What do the five letters of the PALMW method for describing a photo stand for?
cards.answer: Person(en) / Aktion / Location/Ort / Meinung (opinion) / Wetter (weather)

cards.front: Why does the adjective end in -en in 'einen schwarzen Bart' but -e in 'lange blonde Haare'?
cards.answer: After einen (masculine accusative) the adjective adds -en; before a plural noun with no article it adds -e instead.

cards.front: Why does 'ich' come after the verb in 'Im Vordergrund sehe ich einen Mann'?
cards.answer: German main clauses follow the V2 rule: the verb stays in second position, so starting with a location pushes the subject after it.

cards.front: What are the six types of music named in this lesson?
cards.answer: Popmusik (pop) / Rockmusik (rock) / klassische Musik (classical) / Rap/Hip-Hop / elektronische Musik (electronic) / Jazz

cards.front: What are the six types of TV programme named in this lesson?
cards.answer: Seifenoper (soap opera) / Nachrichtensendung (news) / Sportsendung (sports programme) / Quizsendung (quiz show) / Realityshow (reality show) / Serie (series)

cards.front: Why does 'gut' have no ending in 'Der Film ist gut' but become 'guter' in 'ein guter Film'?
cards.answer: An adjective after the verb, in predicative position, takes no ending; before a noun it must take a matching ending.

cards.front: Why does a masculine adjective end in -er in 'ein lustiger Film' but -en in 'einen tollen Film'?
cards.answer: Masculine nominative adjectives after ein add -er, but after einen in the accusative they add -en instead.

cards.front: What are the four connecting words given for linking weather and holiday activities?
cards.answer: weil (because) / deshalb/deswegen (therefore) / als (when — past) / wenn (when/if — present or future)

cards.front: When do you use als instead of wenn when talking about the weather on holiday?
cards.answer: Als is for one single event in the past, while wenn is for repeated events or present/future situations.

cards.front: How do you change 'Es ist sonnig' to describe weather in the past or future?
cards.answer: Change ist to war for the past (Es war sonnig) or add wird for the future (Es wird regnen).

cards.front: What are the three courses of a meal named in this lesson?
cards.answer: die Vorspeise (starter) / das Hauptgericht (main course) / der Nachtisch/die Nachspeise (dessert)

cards.front: What are the five key past participles for food given in this lesson?
cards.answer: essen → gegessen (eaten) / trinken → getrunken (drunk) / bestellen → bestellt (ordered) / finden → gefunden (found) / schmecken → geschmeckt (tasted)

cards.front: Why do you use 'Ich möchte' or 'Ich hätte gern' rather than a direct demand when ordering food?
cards.answer: Ich möchte and Ich hätte gern are polite conditional forms, more courteous than a direct demand, for ordering in a restaurant.

cards.front: How do you say you liked, or didn't like, the taste of a meal using schmecken?
cards.answer: Say es hat mir geschmeckt for I liked the taste, or es hat mir nicht geschmeckt for I didn't.

cards.front: What are the five things a strong paragraph about your best friend should include, in order?
items: their name and how long you've known them
why they're a good friend, using weil
cards.answer: their name and how long you've known them / their personality / what they look like / why they're a good friend, using weil / a balanced detail, using obwohl/trotzdem

cards.front: What are the six bad-friend traits given in this lesson?
cards.answer: ungeduldig (impatient) / eifersüchtig (jealous) / ärgerlich (annoying) / negativ (negative) / langweilig (boring) / gemein (mean)

cards.front: Why doesn't denn send the verb to the end of the clause, unlike weil?
cards.answer: Denn is a coordinating conjunction, not a subordinating one like weil, so it does not change the normal word order.

cards.front: How does trotzdem behave differently from obwohl in a German sentence?
cards.answer: Trotzdem is an adverb, not a conjunction; it starts a new sentence, and the verb comes immediately after it.

cards.front: What are the five German reflexive pronouns given in this lesson, with their meanings?
cards.answer: mich (myself) / dich (yourself) / sich (himself/herself/themselves) / uns (ourselves) / euch (yourselves)

cards.front: What are the six advantages of technology given in this lesson?
cards.answer: stay in contact with friends / find information quickly / it's fun / download music / practical and useful / share videos with friends

cards.front: Where does zu go in the um...zu construction when the verb is separable, as in herunterladen?
cards.answer: With a separable verb, zu is inserted between the prefix and the stem, as in herunterzuladen.

cards.front: How does herunterladen change in the perfect tense, as in 'Ich habe das Video heruntergeladen'?
cards.answer: In the perfect tense, ge- is inserted between the separable prefix and the stem: herunter + ge + laden.

cards.front: What are the five past participles for talking about celebrations given in this lesson?
cards.answer: feiern → gefeiert (celebrated) / dekorieren → dekoriert (decorated) / einladen → eingeladen (invited) / schenken → geschenkt (given as a gift) / sich verkleiden → sich verkleidet (dressed up)

cards.front: What are the four useful celebration phrase-starters given in this lesson?
items: Mein Lieblingsfest ist... (my favourite festival is)
Wir feiern... mit der Familie (we celebrate with)
Es gibt viele Traditionen (there are many traditions)
Das Beste an... ist... (the best thing about)
cards.answer: Mein Lieblingsfest ist... (my favourite festival is) / Wir feiern... mit der Familie (we celebrate with) / Es gibt viele Traditionen (there are many traditions) / Das Beste an... ist... (the best thing about)

cards.front: What are the five discourse markers given for making a balanced argument?
cards.answer: Einerseits (on one hand) / Andererseits (on the other hand) / Außerdem (furthermore) / Jedoch (however) / Trotzdem (nevertheless)

cards.front: What are the six conditional verbs covered in this lesson, with their meanings?
cards.answer: möchte (would like) / würde (would) / hätte (would have) / wäre (would be) / sollte (should) / müsste (must)

cards.front: Why don't hätte and wäre need an infinitive at the end of the sentence, unlike würde?
cards.answer: Hätte and wäre are standalone conditional verbs that carry full meaning alone, so they don't need an infinitive.

cards.front: What is the word order pattern for using möchte, as in 'Ich möchte in zehn Jahren heiraten'?
cards.answer: You conjugate möchten, add any other information, then place the infinitive verb at the very end.

cards.front: What are the three main meals of the day named in this lesson?
cards.answer: das Frühstück (breakfast) / das Mittagessen (lunch) / das Abendessen (dinner)

cards.front: What are the three portion words in the -mal system given in this lesson?
cards.answer: einmal (one portion) / zweimal (two portions) / dreimal (three portions)

cards.front: Why does essen change to isst in 'Mein Bruder isst nicht gern Gemüse'?
cards.answer: Essen is a strong verb, so the e in the stem changes to i in the du and er/sie forms.

cards.front: Why is 'Ich gern Cola' incorrect, while 'Ich trinke gern Cola' is correct?
cards.answer: Gern and its variants must follow a conjugated verb; German needs a verb before the adverb of manner can appear.

cards.front: How do the definite articles change in the dative case in this lesson?
cards.answer: der → dem / das → dem / die → der / die (plural) → den + n

cards.front: What are the six useful phrase-starters given for describing your home?
items: Mein Haus/Meine Wohnung hat... (my house/flat has)
Im Erdgeschoss gibt es... (on the ground floor)
Im ersten Stock... (on the first floor)
Mein Lieblingszimmer ist... (my favourite room is)
Ich teile mein Zimmer... (I share my room)
Ich möchte mein Zimmer renovieren (renovate my room)
cards.answer: Mein Haus/Meine Wohnung hat... (my house/flat has) / Im Erdgeschoss gibt es... (on the ground floor) / Im ersten Stock... (on the first floor) / Mein Lieblingszimmer ist... (my favourite room is) / Ich teile mein Zimmer... (I share my room) / Ich möchte mein Zimmer renovieren (renovate my room)

cards.front: Why does 'in dem Schlafzimmer' use the dative case in 'Die Lampe ist in dem Schlafzimmer'?
cards.answer: Two-way prepositions take the dative case when describing location, where something is, rather than movement.

cards.front: Why are das Schlafzimmer and das Wohnzimmer both neuter, despite different first parts?
cards.answer: German compound nouns take the gender of their last word, and Zimmer (room) is neuter, so both are neuter.

title: Customs and Daily Life in German-Speaking Countries

cards.front: What are the five regional greetings for 'hello' given in this lesson?
cards.answer: Guten Tag (standard formal) / Hallo (informal) / Grüß Gott (southern Germany/Austria) / Moin/Moin Moin (northern Germany) / Grüezi (Swiss German)

cards.front: What are the five rubbish bins Germans separate their waste into, according to this lesson?
cards.answer: Restmüll (general waste) / Bioabfall (organic waste) / Papier (paper) / Gelber Sack (packaging/plastics) / Glas (glass)

cards.front: When do you use Sie instead of du when addressing someone in German?
cards.answer: Use Sie, the formal you, with adults you don't know well, teachers and in professional settings; du is for friends and family.

cards.front: What are the four key conditional forms given in this lesson for talking about celebrities?
items: Ich würde gern... treffen (I'd like to meet)
Ich wäre gern berühmt (want to be famous)
Ich möchte... werden (I'd like to become)
cards.answer: Ich würde gern... treffen (I'd like to meet) / Ich wäre gern berühmt (want to be famous) / Er/Sie würde... (he/she would) / Ich möchte... werden (I'd like to become)

cards.front: What are the four advanced opinion structures given in this lesson?
items: Einerseits... andererseits... (on one hand... on the other)
Ich bin der Meinung, dass... (I believe that)
Nicht nur... sondern auch... (not only... but also)
cards.answer: Einerseits... andererseits... (on one hand... on the other) / Ich bin der Meinung, dass... (I believe that) / Obwohl..., finde ich... (although..., I find) / Nicht nur... sondern auch... (not only... but also)

cards.front: What are the six problems with living in an area given in this lesson?
items: nicht genug für junge Leute (nothing for youth)
Busse fahren nicht oft genug (buses too infrequent)
cards.answer: zu viel Verkehr (too much traffic) / nicht genug für junge Leute (nothing for youth) / Busse fahren nicht oft genug (buses too infrequent) / zu viel Lärm (too much noise) / Probleme mit Müll (rubbish problems) / zu teure Mieten (rents too expensive)

cards.front: Which three short adjectives add an umlaut in the comparative, according to this lesson?
cards.answer: groß → größer (bigger) / alt → älter (older) / klein → kleiner (smaller)

cards.front: What is the difference between so...wie and genauso...wie when comparing two things?
cards.answer: So...wie means 'as...as'; genauso...wie means 'just as...as', a slightly stronger equal comparison.

cards.front: How do you say what you can do in your town in German, using man?
cards.answer: Use man, an impersonal 'you/one', plus kann, as in 'Man kann im Park spazieren gehen' (you can walk in the park).

cards.front: Which four monosyllabic adjectives gain an umlaut in the comparative, according to this lesson?
cards.answer: warm → wärmer / kalt → kälter / gesund → gesünder / scharf → schärfer

cards.front: What are the five key past participles for food given in this lesson?
cards.answer: essen → gegessen (ate) / trinken → getrunken (drank) / bestellen → bestellt (ordered) / kochen → gekocht (cooked) / finden → gefunden (found)

cards.front: Why is 'leckerer' correct for 'tastier' in German, rather than 'mehr lecker'?
cards.answer: German comparatives always add -er to the adjective; mehr (more) is never placed before the adjective, unlike in English.

cards.front: Why does gut become besser in the comparative, rather than gutter or guter?
cards.answer: Gut is completely irregular in the comparative; it becomes besser, just as good becomes better in English.

cards.front: What are the four advanced opinion structures given in this lesson for discussing social media?
items: Ich bin der Meinung, dass... (I believe that)
Ich würde sagen, dass... (I would say that)
Obwohl ich... finde ich... (although..., I find)
Wenn ich könnte, würde ich... (if I could)
cards.answer: Ich bin der Meinung, dass... (I believe that) / Ich würde sagen, dass... (I would say that) / Obwohl ich... finde ich... (although..., I find) / Wenn ich könnte, würde ich... (if I could)

cards.front: What are the three cyberbullying-related phrases given in this lesson?
items: ein Foto ohne Erlaubnis posten (post without permission)
cards.answer: jemanden online mobben (bully someone online) / gemeine Kommentare schreiben (write mean comments) / ein Foto ohne Erlaubnis posten (post without permission)

cards.front: Why is das Handy called a 'false friend' for English speakers?
cards.answer: Das Handy means mobile phone in German, not 'handy' as in useful, despite looking like the English word.

cards.front: How does 'einerseits...andererseits' create a balanced argument about social media, according to this lesson?
cards.answer: Einerseits introduces one side of an argument, and andererseits introduces the opposing side, giving a balanced view.

cards.front: What are the five rubbish bins named in this lesson's Mülltrennung system?
cards.answer: Papier (paper) / Plastik (plastic) / Glas (glass) / Biomüll (organic waste) / Restmüll (general waste)

cards.front: What are the four discourse markers given in this lesson for balanced arguments?
cards.answer: Einerseits (on one hand) / andererseits (on the other hand) / Zwar (admittedly) / aber (but)

cards.front: How can you work out the meaning of Umweltverschmutzung without knowing the whole word?
cards.answer: Break the compound noun into its parts: Umwelt (environment) plus Verschmutzung (pollution), giving 'environmental pollution'.

cards.front: How do you form the future tense to say what will happen to the environment?
cards.answer: Use a form of werden plus the infinitive, which goes to the end of the clause, as in 'wird...schlimmer werden'.

cards.front: What are the four main ways given in this lesson to talk about pain or injury?
items: Ich habe Kopfschmerzen (I have a headache)
Ich leide an Zahnschmerzen (I suffer toothache)
Ich habe mir den Finger gebrochen (finger broken)
Ich habe mir das Bein verletzt (leg injured)
cards.answer: Ich habe Kopfschmerzen (I have a headache) / Ich leide an Zahnschmerzen (I suffer toothache) / Ich habe mir den Finger gebrochen (finger broken) / Ich habe mir das Bein verletzt (leg injured)

cards.front: Which four strong verbs change their vowel in the du and er/sie forms, according to this lesson?
cards.answer: laufen → läuft (a→ä) / fahren → fährt (a→ä) / schlafen → schläft (a→ä) / lesen → liest (e→ie)

cards.front: How do you decide whether to use haben or sein in the perfect tense, according to this lesson?
cards.answer: Use sein for verbs of a change of location, like swimming or running; use haben for everything else, like eating.

cards.front: What is the 'sandwich pattern' word order for a sentence with a modal verb, like müssen?
cards.answer: The subject comes first, the modal verb second, extra information in the middle, and the infinitive verb at the very end.

cards.front: What are the four words used to build conversational time expressions in German?
cards.answer: nach (past) / vor (to) / Viertel (quarter) / halb (half to)

cards.front: What are the six day-adverbs given in this lesson for talking about your timetable?
cards.answer: montags (on Mondays) / dienstags (on Tuesdays) / mittwochs (on Wednesdays) / donnerstags (on Thursdays) / freitags (on Fridays) / täglich (daily)

cards.front: Why does 'halb sechs' mean 5:30 rather than 6:30 in German?
cards.answer: Halb means 'half to' the next hour in German, not 'half past', so halb sechs is half to six, 5:30.

cards.front: Why does 'ich' come after 'habe' in 'Montags habe ich Englisch'?
cards.answer: German follows the verb-second rule: starting with a time phrase pushes the subject after the verb, called inversion.

cards.front: What are the five types of German secondary school named in this lesson?
cards.answer: das Gymnasium (grammar school) / die Realschule (middle school) / die Hauptschule (vocational-track school) / die Gesamtschule (comprehensive) / die Grundschule (primary school)

cards.front: What is the word order pattern for a school-rule sentence like 'Man darf im Gang nicht laufen'?
cards.answer: The modal verb comes first, after man, then extra information such as location, then the infinitive verb at the very end.

cards.front: Why does 'ist' move to the end in 'Ich denke, dass die Schuluniform wichtig ist'?
cards.answer: Dass is a subordinating conjunction, like weil and obwohl, so it sends the verb to the end of its clause.
